newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle des Eaux, Havas move on Canal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gle des Eaux, Havas move on Canal - paper.

text.p: French conglomerate Cie Generale des Eaux is set to move its 20.4 percent holding in pay TV company Canal Plus into media group Havas in an operation which would leave Havas with 43.5 percent of Canal Plus, Le Figaro said in an unsourced article in its weekend edition.
The newspaper said none of those involved would comment.

The operation would mean Havas still controlled less than the 49 percent stake which would require a takeover offer for Canal Plus and it would compensate Generale des Eaux via a reserved capital increase, said the newspaper.

Le Figaro said the other part of the operation would involve Generale des Eaux buying part of Alcatel Alsthom's 's stake in Canal Plus, leaving Alcatel with around 10 percent of the capital of Canal Plus.
Le Monde, which ran an interview with Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier in its weekend edition, said Dauzier declined to comment when asked about the article appearing in Le Figaro.
Back in October, Havas finance director Nicolas Duhamel told an analysts' meeting his group would raise its stake in Canal Plus with the agreement of Generale des Eaux.
"There is no rush in increasing our participation. It will be done in consultation with Generale des Eaux when it gets done," Duhamel said at the time.
Havas's stake in Canal Plus would be diluted by a merger between the subscriber TV station and Nethold and Havas wanted to bring it back up to pre-merger level, he said at the time.
Canal Plus said in September it was merging with Nethold, jointly owned by Richemont SA and MIH Holdings.
